skill.name: create-unit-test
skill.description: Helps create Kotlin unit tests for Android modules using project naming, source-set, Robolectric, and Gradle conventions.
skill.summary: Guides Android unit test planning, file placement, implementation, execution, and failure review.
skill.author: AnySoftKeyboard

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown inline code or project guidance, not executable code. The Gradle command instructions are confirmed as medium-risk external command guidance because ./gradlew can execute repository-controlled build logic. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: State that agents must ask user confirmation before running ./gradlew and run it only in trusted workspaces.
Prefer the narrow module test task and avoid broader Gradle test commands unless the user requests them.

content.value_statement: Android projects need unit tests that follow local module, runner, and naming rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through planning, writing, and running those tests.
actual_capabilities: Plans unit tests by identifying happy paths, error cases, and edge cases.
Places Kotlin test files under the module test source set.
Recommends Robolectric for Android component tests.
Guides test implementation with Arrange, Act, Assert structure.
Runs or recommends Gradle unit test commands for the target module.
Uses XML test result paths to locate failing test details.
limitations: It is tailored to Android and Kotlin projects that use Gradle.
It does not define full implementation details unless the user asks.
It may run local Gradle commands, which can execute project build logic.
It does not cover instrumentation tests except as a rare exception.

use_cases.title: Add focused unit coverage
use_cases.description: Create tests for a class while following module paths, naming rules, and source-set conventions.

use_cases.title: Validate behavior cases
use_cases.description: Turn happy paths, error cases, and likely edge cases into a clear test plan.

use_cases.title: Review test failures
use_cases.description: Run the correct Gradle unit test task and inspect XML reports when tests fail.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a unit test for this Android Kotlin class. Follow the project naming and test source-set rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan behavior coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this class and propose happy path, error case, and edge case tests before creating the test file.

prompt_templates.title: Use Robolectric correctly
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Robolectric unit test for this Android component and keep resources deterministic.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a failing test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced failure review after a Gradle run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failing unit test result, identify the cause, and suggest the smallest behavior-focused fix.

output_examples.input: A user asks for tests for a Kotlin class with normal and invalid inputs.
output: A correctly named test file in the module test source set.
Clear assertions for happy path and error behavior.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to run the new Android unit test.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the module test task and explains where the XML result report will appear.

output_examples.input: A Robolectric test fails because an Android resource is missing.
output_examples.output: The skill guides review of the failure report and recommends deterministic resource setup.

best_practices: Review source behavior before writing assertions.
Prefer fakes over mocks when they keep tests clear.
Run the narrow module test task after adding or changing tests.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation-detail assertions before behavior is understood.
Putting unit tests under androidTest when instrumentation is not needed.
Running broad Gradle tasks in an untrusted repository without user approval.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Android and Kotlin projects that use Gradle unit tests.

faq.question: Does it create Robolectric tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Robolectric when the test covers Android components.

faq.question: Where does it place test files?
faq.answer: It places tests in the module test source set under the matching package path.

faq.question: Can it run tests?
faq.answer: It can guide or run Gradle unit test commands when the user permits command execution.

faq.question: Does it prefer mocks?
faq.answer: No. It prefers fakes and uses mocks only when fakes are too complex.

faq.question: Does it handle flaky tests?
faq.answer: It encourages deterministic tests and failure review through Gradle XML reports.
